sanskrit: svayaṃ prahartādātā ca vaśyātmā vaśyasādhanaḥ kāle dātā ca bhoktā ca śuddhācāras tathaiva ca
english: He should strike in his own person and seize, his self under control and his instruments under control; a giver in season and an enjoyer in season, and a man of pure conduct as well.

sanskrit: śūrān bhaktān asaṃhāryān kule jātān arogiṇaḥ śiṣṭāñ śiṣṭābhisaṃbandhān mānino nāvamāninaḥ
english: Let him take as allies men who are valiant, loyal, not to be bought away, well-born, free of disease, refined and allied with the refined, self-respecting and not contemptuous of others.

sanskrit: vidyāvido lokavidaḥ paralokānvavekṣakān dharmeṣu niratān sādhūn acalān acalān iva
english: Men learned in knowledge, knowing the ways of the world, mindful of the world beyond, devoted to the duties of dharma, good, and as unshakable as mountains.

sanskrit: sahāyān satataṃ kuryād rājā bhūtipuraskṛtaḥ tais tulyaś ca bhaved bhogaiś chatramātrājñayādhikaḥ
english: Such men the king should ever make his companions, keeping their welfare foremost. He should be their equal in enjoyments, exalted above them only by the royal parasol and the power of command.

sanskrit: pratyakṣā ca parokṣā ca vṛttiś cāsya bhavet sadā evaṃ kṛtvā narendro hi na khedam iha vindati
english: His conduct, both seen and unseen, should at all times be the same. Acting thus, the lord of men finds no grief in this world.

sanskrit: sarvātiśaṅkī nṛpatir yaś ca sarvaharo bhavet sa kṣipram anṛjur lubdhaḥ svajanenaiva bādhyate
english: But a king who suspects everyone and seizes everything—crooked and greedy—is soon brought to ruin by his own people.

sanskrit: śucis tu pṛthivīpālo lokacittagrahe rataḥ na pataty aribhir grastaḥ patitaś cāvatiṣṭhate
english: The pure guardian of the earth, devoted to winning the hearts of his people, does not fall though seized by foes; and if he falls, he rises again.

sanskrit: akrodhano 'thāvyasanī mṛdudaṇḍo jitendriyaḥ rājā bhavati bhūtānāṃ viśvāsyo himavān iva
english: Free of anger, free of vice, gentle in punishment, his senses mastered—such a king becomes as trustworthy to his creatures as the Himālaya.

sanskrit: prājño nyāyaguṇopetaḥ pararandhreṣu tatparaḥ sudarśaḥ sarvavarṇānāṃ nayāpanayavit tathā
english: Wise, endowed with the virtues of justice, intent upon the weak points of his enemies, fair to look upon for all the classes, and knowing both policy and the failure of policy.

sanskrit: kṣiprakārī jitakrodhaḥ suprasādo mahāmanāḥ arogaprakṛtir yuktaḥ kriyāvān avikatthanaḥ
english: Swift in action, his anger conquered, readily gracious, magnanimous, of healthy constitution, disciplined, energetic in his undertakings, and not given to boasting.

sanskrit: ārabdhāny eva kāryāṇi na paryavasitāni ca yasya rājñaḥ pradṛśyante sa rājā rājasattamaḥ
english: The king whose enterprises are seen to be begun but never yet finished off—that king is the best of kings.

sanskrit: putrā iva pitur gehe viṣaye yasya mānavāḥ nirbhayā vicariṣyanti sa rājā rājasattamaḥ
english: He in whose realm men move about without fear, like sons in their father's house—that king is the best of kings.

sanskrit: agūḍhavibhavā yasya paurā rāṣṭranivāsinaḥ nayāpanayavettāraḥ sa rājā rājasattamaḥ
english: He whose townsfolk and country-dwellers do not have to hide their wealth, and who discern between sound and unsound policy—that king is the best of kings.

sanskrit: svakarmaniratā yasya janā viṣayavāsinaḥ asaṃghātaratā dāntāḥ pālyamānā yathāvidhi
english: He whose people, dwelling in his realm, are devoted each to his own work, taking no pleasure in conspiracy, self-restrained, and protected according to the ordinances—

sanskrit: vaśyā neyā vinītāś ca na ca saṃgharṣaśīlinaḥ viṣaye dānarucayo narā yasya sa pārthivaḥ
english: obedient, biddable, well-disciplined, not given to strife, and delighting in giving within his realm—he is a true king.

sanskrit: na yasya kūṭakapaṭaṃ na māyā na ca matsaraḥ viṣaye bhūmipālasya tasya dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: In whose realm there is no trickery or deceit, no fraud, no envy—that guardian of the earth holds dharma eternal.

sanskrit: yaḥ satkaroti jñānāni neyaḥ paurahite rataḥ satāṃ dharmānugas tyāgī sa rājā rājyam arhati
english: He who honors the sciences, is amenable to counsel, devoted to the welfare of his townsfolk, follows the dharma of the good, and is liberal—that king deserves his kingdom.

sanskrit: yasya cāraś ca mantraś ca nityaṃ caiva kṛtākṛte na jñāyate hi ripubhiḥ sa rājā rājyam arhati
english: He whose spies, whose counsel, and whose deeds done and undone are never known to his foes—that king deserves his kingdom.

sanskrit: ślokaś cāyaṃ purā gīto bhārgaveṇa mahātmanā ākhyāte rāmacarite nṛpatiṃ prati bhārata
english: And this verse was once sung by the great-souled descendant of Bhṛgu, in the telling of the deeds of Rāma, concerning the king, O Bhārata:

sanskrit: rājānaṃ prathamaṃ vindet tato bhāryāṃ tato dhanam rājany asati lokasya kuto bhāryā kuto dhanam
english: "First let a man find a king, then a wife, then wealth. When there is no king, whence comes a wife for the world, and whence comes wealth?"

sanskrit: tad rājan rājasiṃhānāṃ nānyo dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ ṛte rakṣāṃ suvispaṣṭāṃ rakṣā lokasya dhāraṇam
english: Therefore, O king, for the lions among kings there is no other eternal dharma than plain and manifest protection; protection is the sustaining of the world.

sanskrit: prācetasena manunā ślokau cemāv udāhṛtau rājadharmeṣu rājendra tāv ihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu
english: And these two verses were uttered by Manu, son of Pracetas, concerning the duties of kings, O lord of kings; hear them now with single-minded attention.

sanskrit: ṣaḍ etān puruṣo jahyād bhinnāṃ nāvam ivārṇave apravaktāram ācāryam anadhīyānam ṛtvijam
english: "These six a man should abandon, as one abandons a leaking boat upon the sea: a teacher who does not teach, an officiating priest who has not studied,

sanskrit: arakṣitāraṃ rājānaṃ bhāryāṃ cāpriyavādinīm grāmakāmaṃ ca gopālaṃ vanakāmaṃ ca nāpitam
english: a king who does not protect, a wife of unkind speech, a cowherd who longs for the village, and a barber who longs for the forest."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca etat te rājadharmāṇāṃ navanītaṃ yudhiṣṭhira bṛhaspatir hi bhagavān nānyaṃ dharmaṃ praśaṃsati
english: Bhīṣma said: This is the very cream of the duties of kings that I have given you, Yudhiṣṭhira; for the venerable Bṛhaspati commends no other dharma.

sanskrit: viśālākṣaś ca bhagavān kāvyaś caiva mahātapāḥ sahasrākṣo mahendraś ca tathā prācetaso manuḥ
english: The venerable Viśālākṣa, and Kāvya of great austerities, and the thousand-eyed great Indra, and Manu son of Pracetas,

sanskrit: bharadvājaś ca bhagavāṃs tathā gauraśirā muniḥ rājaśāstrapraṇetāro brahmaṇyā brahmavādinaḥ
english: and the venerable Bharadvāja, and the sage Gauraśiras—these authors of the science of kingcraft, devoted to brahman and expounders of brahman,

sanskrit: rakṣām eva praśaṃsanti dharmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ vara rājñāṃ rājīvatāmrākṣa sādhanaṃ cātra vai śṛṇu
english: commend protection alone as the dharma of kings, O best of upholders of dharma, you whose eyes are coppery as the lotus. And now hear of the means to achieve it.

sanskrit: cāraś ca praṇidhiś caiva kāle dānam amatsaraḥ yuktyādānaṃ na cādānam ayogena yudhiṣṭhira
english: Spies and secret agents, giving in season without envy, taking by right means but not seizing by wrong ones, O Yudhiṣṭhira—

sanskrit: satāṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ śauryaṃ dākṣyaṃ satyaṃ prajāhitam anārjavair ārjavaiś ca śatrupakṣasya bhedanam
english: the gathering of good men, valor, skill, truth, the welfare of the subjects, and the breaking up of the enemy's faction by crooked means and by straight—

sanskrit: sādhūnām aparityāgaḥ kulīnānāṃ ca dhāraṇam nicayaś ca niceyānāṃ sevā buddhimatām api
english: not forsaking the good, sustaining the well-born, laying up what should be laid up, and the service of the wise as well—

sanskrit: balānāṃ harṣaṇaṃ nityaṃ prajānām anvavekṣaṇam kāryeṣv akhedaḥ kośasya tathaiva ca vivardhanam
english: the constant heartening of his troops, the watching over of his subjects, tirelessness in his undertakings, and the increasing of the treasury—

sanskrit: puraguptir aviśvāsaḥ paurasaṃghātabhedanam ketanānāṃ ca jīrṇānām avekṣā caiva sīdatām
english: the guarding of the city, wariness, the breaking up of conspiracies among the townsfolk, and attention to dilapidated dwellings and to those who are sinking into ruin—

sanskrit: dvividhasya ca daṇḍasya prayogaḥ kālacoditaḥ arimadhyasthamitrāṇāṃ yathāvac cānvavekṣaṇam
english: the application, urged by the occasion, of the two kinds of punishment, and the proper watching over enemies, neutrals, and friends—

sanskrit: upajāpaś ca bhṛtyānām ātmanaḥ paradarśanāt aviśvāsaḥ svayaṃ caiva parasyāśvāsanaṃ tathā
english: the suborning of the enemy's servants, and—from observing how others fare—being himself distrustful, while reassuring the other side—

sanskrit: nītidharmānusaraṇaṃ nityam utthānam eva ca ripūṇām anavajñānaṃ nityaṃ cānāryavarjanam
english: following the dharma of statecraft, constant exertion, never despising one's foes, and ever shunning the ignoble:

sanskrit: utthānaṃ hi narendrāṇāṃ bṛhaspatir abhāṣata rājadharmasya yan mūlaṃ ślokāṃś cātra nibodha me
english: For Bṛhaspati declared that exertion is the very root of the kings' dharma; learn from me the verses upon this.

sanskrit: utthānenāmṛtaṃ labdham utthānenāsurā hatāḥ utthānena mahendreṇa śraiṣṭhyaṃ prāptaṃ divīha ca
english: By exertion the nectar of immortality was won; by exertion the Asuras were slain; by exertion the great Indra attained supremacy in heaven and on earth.

sanskrit: utthānadhīraḥ puruṣo vāgdhīrān adhitiṣṭhati utthānadhīraṃ vāgdhīrā ramayanta upāsate
english: The man steadfast in action stands above those steadfast only in speech; the men steadfast in speech wait upon and please the one steadfast in action.

sanskrit: utthānahīno rājā hi buddhimān api nityaśaḥ dharṣaṇīyo ripūṇāṃ syād bhujaṃga iva nirviṣaḥ
english: For a king devoid of exertion, however wise he be, is forever there for his foes to trample, like a serpent stripped of its venom.

sanskrit: na ca śatrur avajñeyo durbalo 'pi balīyasā alpo 'pi hi dahaty agnir viṣam alpaṃ hinasti ca
english: And an enemy is not to be despised by the stronger, even though he be weak; for even a small fire burns, and a little poison kills.

sanskrit: ekāśvenāpi saṃbhūtaḥ śatrur durgasamāśritaḥ taṃ taṃ tāpayate deśam api rājñaḥ samṛddhinaḥ
english: An enemy possessed of but a single horse, taking refuge in a stronghold, can scorch this region and that even of a prosperous king.

sanskrit: rājño rahasyaṃ yad vākyaṃ jayārthaṃ lokasaṃgrahaḥ hṛdi yac cāsya jihmaṃ syāt kāraṇārthaṃ ca yad bhavet
english: The secret counsel of a king for the sake of victory, his gathering of allies, whatever crookedness may be in his heart and whatever serves his purpose—

sanskrit: yac cāsya kāryaṃ vṛjinam ārjavenaiva dhāryate dambhanārthāya lokasya dharmiṣṭhām ācaret kriyām
english: whatever crooked deed of his is to be carried out, he should sustain it under a show of straightforwardness, and to deceive the world he should perform the most righteous-seeming acts.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ hi sumahat tantraṃ durdhāryam akṛtātmabhiḥ na śakyaṃ mṛdunā voḍhum āghātasthānam uttamam
english: For kingship is a vast machine, hard to be borne by the undisciplined; it cannot be carried by a gentle man—it is a supreme place of slaughter.

sanskrit: rājyaṃ sarvāmiṣaṃ nityam ārjaveneha dhāryate tasmān miśreṇa satataṃ vartitavyaṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: Kingship, that bait coveted by all, can never be held in this world by straightforwardness alone; therefore one must ever act by a blend of both, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yady apy asya vipattiḥ syād rakṣamāṇasya vai prajāḥ so 'py asya vipulo dharma evaṃvṛttā hi bhūmipāḥ
english: And even should disaster befall him while he protects his subjects, that too is great dharma for him; for such is the conduct of the guardians of the earth.

sanskrit: eṣa te rājadharmāṇāṃ leśaḥ samanuvarṇitaḥ bhūyas te yatra saṃdehas tad brūhi vadatāṃ vara
english: This much of the duties of kings I have set forth to you in brief; whatever further doubt you have, speak it, O best of speakers.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato vyāsaś ca bhagavān devasthāno 'śmanā saha vāsudevaḥ kṛpaś caiva sātyakiḥ saṃjayas tathā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the venerable Vyāsa, and Devasthāna together with Aśman, and Vāsudeva, and Kṛpa, and Sātyaki, and Saṃjaya likewise—

sanskrit: sādhu sādhv iti saṃhṛṣṭāḥ puṣyamāṇair ivānanaiḥ astuvaṃs te naravyāghraṃ bhīṣmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ varam
english: crying "Well said, well said!" and thrilled with joy, their faces as it were abloom, they praised that tiger among men, Bhīṣma, the best of the upholders of dharma.

sanskrit: tato dīnamanā bhīṣmam uvāca kurusattamaḥ netrābhyām aśrupūrṇābhyāṃ pādau tasya śanaiḥ spṛśan
english: Then with downcast heart that best of the Kurus spoke to Bhīṣma, gently touching his feet, his eyes brimming with tears:

sanskrit: śva idānīṃ svasaṃdehaṃ prakṣyāmi tvaṃ pitāmaha upaiti savitāpy astaṃ rasam āpīya pārthivam
english: "Tomorrow now I shall ask you of my doubts, grandsire; the sun too is going to its setting, having drunk up the earth's moisture."

sanskrit: tato dvijātīn abhivādya keśavaḥ; kṛpaś ca te caiva yudhiṣṭhirādayaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya mahānadīsutaṃ; tato rathān āruruhur mudā yutāḥ
english: Then Keśava and Kṛpa, and Yudhiṣṭhira and the others, having saluted the twice-born and circumambulated the son of the great river, mounted their chariots filled with gladness.

sanskrit: dṛṣadvatīṃ cāpy avagāhya suvratāḥ; kṛtodakāryāḥ kṛtajapyamaṅgalāḥ upāsya saṃdhyāṃ vidhivat paraṃtapās; tataḥ puraṃ te viviśur gajāhvayam
english: And those firm in their vows, those scorchers of foes, having bathed in the Dṛṣadvatī, performed the water-rites, and made their auspicious recitations, and having worshipped the twilight according to the ordinance, then entered the city named for the elephant.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ kālyaṃ samutthāya kṛtapaurvāhṇikakriyāḥ yayus te nagarākārai rathaiḥ pāṇḍavayādavāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, rising at daybreak and performing the morning rites, the Pāṇḍavas and the Yādavas went forth in chariots vast as cities.

sanskrit: prapadya ca kurukṣetraṃ bhīṣmam āsādya cānagham sukhāṃ ca rajanīṃ pṛṣṭvā gāṅgeyaṃ rathināṃ varam
english: And reaching Kurukṣetra and coming to the sinless Bhīṣma, son of Gaṅgā, best of charioteers, they asked whether his night had passed in ease.

sanskrit: vyāsādīn abhivādyarṣīn sarvais taiś cābhinanditāḥ niṣedur abhito bhīṣmaṃ parivārya samantataḥ
english: Having saluted the seers, Vyāsa and the rest, and being greeted by them all, they sat down all around Bhīṣma, surrounding him on every side.

sanskrit: tato rājā mahātejā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ abravīt prāñjalir bhīṣmaṃ pratipūjyābhivādya ca
english: Then the king of great splendor, Yudhiṣṭhira the Dharmarāja, having honored and saluted Bhīṣma, spoke to him with joined palms:

sanskrit: ya eṣa rājā-rājeti śabdaś carati bhārata katham eṣa samutpannas tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: "This word that goes about, 'king, king,' O Bhārata—how did it first arise? Tell me that, grandsire.

sanskrit: tulyapāṇiśirogrīvas tulyabuddhīndriyātmakaḥ tulyaduḥkhasukhātmā ca tulyapṛṣṭhabhujodaraḥ
english: Equal in hands, head, and neck, equal in intellect, senses, and self, equal in his capacity for pain and pleasure, equal in back, arms, and belly—

sanskrit: tulyaśukrāsthimajjaś ca tulyamāṃsāsṛg eva ca niḥśvāsocchvāsatulyaś ca tulyaprāṇaśarīravān
english: equal in seed, bone, and marrow, equal too in flesh and blood, equal in his breathing out and in, possessed of a body and life-breath like the rest—

sanskrit: samānajanmamaraṇaḥ samaḥ sarvaguṇair nṛṇām viśiṣṭabuddhīñ śūrāṃś ca katham eko 'dhitiṣṭhati
english: the same in birth and death, the same in all the qualities of men—how does one man stand above those of surpassing intellect and the brave?

sanskrit: katham eko mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ vīraśūrāryasaṃkulām rakṣaty api ca loko 'sya prasādam abhivāñchati
english: How does one man protect the whole earth, thronged with heroes, champions, and noble men—and the world besides yearns for his favor?

sanskrit: ekasya ca prasādena kṛtsno lokaḥ prasīdati vyākulenākulaḥ sarvo bhavatīti viniścayaḥ
english: By the contentment of one man the whole world grows content; when he is troubled, all the world is troubled too—such is the settled truth.

sanskrit: etad icchāmy ahaṃ sarvaṃ tattvena bharatarṣabha śrotuṃ tan me yathātattvaṃ prabrūhi vadatāṃ vara
english: All this I wish to hear truly, O bull of the Bhāratas; expound it to me as it really is, O best of speakers.

sanskrit: naitat kāraṇam alpaṃ hi bhaviṣyati viśāṃ pate yad ekasmiñ jagat sarvaṃ devavad yāti saṃnatim
english: No small cause can this be, O lord of peoples, that before one man the whole world bows down as before a god."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca niyatas tvaṃ naraśreṣṭha śṛṇu sarvam aśeṣataḥ yathā rājyaṃ samutpannam ādau kṛtayuge 'bhavat
english: Bhīṣma said: With self under control, O best of men, hear it all in full—how kingship first arose in the beginning, in the Kṛta age.

sanskrit: naiva rājyaṃ na rājāsīn na daṇḍo na ca dāṇḍikaḥ dharmeṇaiva prajāḥ sarvā rakṣanti ca parasparam
english: There was no kingdom, no king, no punishment, and no one to inflict it; by dharma alone all the people protected one another.

sanskrit: pālayānās tathānyonyaṃ narā dharmeṇa bhārata khedaṃ paramam ājagmus tatas tān moha āviśat
english: But as men guarded one another thus by dharma, O Bhārata, they came at last to utter weariness, and thereupon delusion entered into them.

sanskrit: te mohavaśam āpannā mānavā manujarṣabha pratipattivimohāc ca dharmas teṣām anīnaśat
english: Fallen under the sway of delusion, O bull among men, those men, through the bewildering of their judgment, let their dharma perish.

sanskrit: naṣṭāyāṃ pratipattau tu mohavaśyā narās tadā lobhasya vaśam āpannāḥ sarve bhāratasattama
english: And when their judgment was lost, the men, mastered by delusion, then fell one and all under the sway of greed, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: aprāptasyābhimarśaṃ tu kurvanto manujās tataḥ kāmo nāmāparas tatra samapadyata vai prabho
english: Then, as men reached out to grasp at what was not theirs, another thing called desire arose there among them, O lord.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu kāmavaśaṃ prāptān rāgo nāma samaspṛśat raktāś ca nābhyajānanta kāryākāryaṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: And as they fell under the sway of desire, a thing called passion laid hold of them; impassioned, they no longer knew what should and should not be done, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: agamyāgamanaṃ caiva vācyāvācyaṃ tathaiva ca bhakṣyābhakṣyaṃ ca rājendra doṣādoṣaṃ ca nātyajan
english: Going to those who were forbidden, speaking what was not to be spoken, eating what was not to be eaten, O lord of kings—they shunned neither fault nor virtue.

sanskrit: viplute naraloke 'smiṃs tato brahma nanāśa ha nāśāc ca brahmaṇo rājan dharmo nāśam athāgamat
english: When this world of men was thus thrown into ruin, then the Veda perished; and from the perishing of the Veda, O king, dharma too came to its destruction.

sanskrit: naṣṭe brahmaṇi dharme ca devās trāsam athāgaman te trastā naraśārdūla brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ
english: When the Veda and dharma were lost, the gods then fell into terror; and in their terror, O tiger among men, they went to Brahmā for refuge.

sanskrit: prapadya bhagavantaṃ te devā lokapitāmaham ūcuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve duḥkhaśokabhayārditāḥ
english: Coming to the venerable Brahmā, the grandsire of the world, those gods, all afflicted with grief, sorrow, and fear, spoke with joined palms:

sanskrit: bhagavan naralokasthaṃ naṣṭaṃ brahma sanātanam lobhamohādibhir bhāvais tato no bhayam āviśat
english: "Venerable one, the eternal Veda that dwelt in the world of men is lost through such states as greed and delusion, and thereupon fear has entered into us.

sanskrit: brahmaṇaś ca praṇāśena dharmo 'py anaśad īśvara tataḥ sma samatāṃ yātā martyais tribhuvaneśvara
english: And by the perishing of the Veda, dharma too has perished, O Lord; thereby we have been brought level with mortals, O lord of the three worlds.

sanskrit: adho hi varṣam asmākaṃ martyās tūrdhvapravarṣiṇaḥ kriyāvyuparamāt teṣāṃ tato 'gacchāma saṃśayam
english: For our rain falls downward, but the mortals rain upward by their offerings; and since their rites have ceased, we have thereby fallen into peril."
